sentences.text: Piatnitzkysaurus was a medium-sized theropod dinosaur known for its light frame and strong forelimbs.
While the holotype was a subadult, fully grown adults likely reached a total length of 6.6 meters.
Its head measured 50 centimeters in length and featured large openings that reduced its overall weight.
The creature possessed long, sharp teeth that were conical, highly compressed, and curved backward.
Strong hind legs supported its body, while the front limbs ended in three clawed fingers.
One of the pelvic bones, the ischium, was recorded at a length of 423 millimeters.
The braincase included a parasphenoid recess, a feature shared with only two other non-avian theropods.
Additionally, a prominent hook-like wing on the basisphenoid was present, similar to traits seen in Ceratosaurus and Allosaurus.
This species is unique within its family because it is the only one with preserved skull parts, including two maxillae and a partial lower jaw.
It is also remarkable for having robust arms despite its overall light build and medium size.
The holotype specimen was gathered during fieldwork conducted in 1977, 1982, and 1983 from the Cañadón Asfalto Formation.
The type species Piatnitzkysaurus floresi was formally described by Jose Bonaparte in 1979.
Its light construction would have allowed the animal to move with great speed.
When gripping prey, its claws likely inflicted wounds that caused bleeding until the victim could no longer resist.
The dinosaur belongs to the most basal group within Megalosauroidea, a clade that also includes Condorraptor, Marshosaurus, and Xuanhanosaurus.
It is classified within the family Piatnitzkysauridae.
Piatnitzkysaurus floresi remains the sole known species within this genus of megalosauroid theropod.
Fossil records place the existence of Piatnitzkysaurus in the Toarcian stage, spanning from 182.9 to 180.4 million years ago.
Scientists debate whether Condorraptor represents a distinct species or simply individual variation within Piatnitzkysaurus due to their strong resemblance.
It is also debated whether the placement of Piatnitzkysauridae within Megalosauroidea is correct, as future studies might reclassify them outside this group.
